meta.label: Smart thermostats
meta.attribution: Hand-checked from ENERGY STAR certification records (data.energystar.gov), product pages, privacy policies, App Store privacy labels, security and support-lifecycle notices, smart-home compatibility docs, and independent privacy reviews. A product's support period matters here: Google cut older Nest thermostats off from its apps in October 2025. HVAC compatibility is house-specific; check wiring, voltage, C-wire, boiler type, region, rebates, and installer requirements before buying. Suggest changes via Contribute.

products.name: Sensi Touch 2
products.description: A mainstream ENERGY STAR thermostat with an unusually explicit privacy positioning and broad U.S. HVAC compatibility.

environment.note: ENERGY STAR certifies the Sensi Touch 2 (ST76, qualified June 2022, US and Canada) with time-of-day, geofencing, humidity sensing and extra room-sensor support.

privacy.note: Sensi's public positioning emphasizes data privacy and says Sensi does not sell personal information to third parties.

openness.note: Sensi works through mainstream smart-home integrations rather than an open local-control protocol, so openness is good but not maximal.

transparency.note: Sensi publishes installation, compatibility, privacy, and energy-savings claims in public product materials.

accessibility.note: DIY installation and broad 24V HVAC support help accessibility, but a C-wire may still be required depending on the model and home.

products.name: ecobee Smart Thermostat Premium
products.description: A strong premium option with remote sensors, broad integrations, and better-than-average privacy language for a connected-home product.

environment.note: ENERGY STAR certifies the Smart Thermostat Premium (EB-STATE6, qualified April 2023, US and Canada) with an occupancy sensor on the device, extra occupancy and temperature sensors, outdoor temperature detection, geofencing and ecobee's optional Community Energy Savings demand-response program.

privacy.note: ecobee's privacy notice says 'Your personal information and data belong to you' and offers deletion, but also that ecobee may be treated as selling or sharing data under US state law because it discloses 'certain ecobee Product user data to third parties for their own marketing purposes'. Apple's label lists contact info and user ID linked to you for the developer's marketing.

openness.note: ecobee supports several smart-home ecosystems and voice assistants, which reduces lock-in compared with single-ecosystem thermostats.

transparency.note: Mozilla's privacy review notes ecobee's comparatively strong privacy language while still warning that privacy claims need scrutiny.

accessibility.note: Premium pricing and installation complexity lower accessibility even though the product includes a power-extender kit and rich setup docs.

products.name: tado Smart Thermostat X
products.description: A European smart-heating platform with Matter/Thread support and strong energy-savings claims, best for compatible EU/UK heating systems.

environment.note: tado cites a Fraunhofer Institute report finding up to 28% heating energy savings for tado smart thermostats.

privacy.note: tado's app privacy listing shows location, contact information, identifiers, usage data, and diagnostics may be handled by the app.

openness.note: tado X uses Matter, increasing cross-platform control across iOS, Android, Alexa, Siri, and Google Home ecosystems.

transparency.note: tado publishes support pages for Matter setup and links to terms and privacy policy inside its support system.

accessibility.note: tado X is strong where heating-system compatibility fits, but region, bridge, radiator valve, and subscription-feature choices complicate setup.

products.name: Netatmo Smart Thermostat
products.description: A European smart thermostat with GDPR-region privacy posture and broad assistant compatibility, strongest for compatible boiler systems.

environment.note: Netatmo's energy app and thermostat materials emphasize scheduling and consumption tracking to reduce unnecessary heating.

privacy.note: Mozilla's Netatmo thermostat review highlights GDPR-region protections and notes that Netatmo says it does not sell data.

openness.note: Netatmo publishes HomeKit compatibility support and supports major assistant integrations for its thermostat ecosystem.

transparency.note: Netatmo publishes a dedicated privacy notice for app and product data processing.

accessibility.note: Netatmo is most accessible in compatible European heating setups; regional availability and boiler compatibility can limit fit.

products.name: Google Nest Learning Thermostat
products.description: A polished, recognizable smart thermostat with strong energy features and a major-platform privacy tradeoff.

environment.note: ENERGY STAR certifies the 4th gen Nest Learning Thermostat (GA05 models, qualified April 2024) for the US and Canada market only, with an occupancy sensor on the device, outdoor temperature detection, geofencing and Google's opt-out utility demand-response service.

privacy.note: Google Home and Nest privacy documentation says Nest device data is handled under Google account and Google privacy systems.

openness.note: Nest supports the Google Home ecosystem and some wider integrations, but it remains heavily tied to Google's smart-home account model.

transparency.note: Google publishes Nest privacy commitments and sensor-use explanations, making the data model more inspectable than many smart-home products.

accessibility.note: Nest is widely available and user-friendly, but HVAC compatibility and Google-account dependence should be checked before purchase.

products.name: Honeywell Home T9
products.description: A familiar room-sensor thermostat with ENERGY STAR certification and broad assistant support, but Resideo account/app dependence.

environment.note: ENERGY STAR lists Honeywell Home T9 thermostat families as certified connected thermostats with demand-response capability.

privacy.note: Resideo's connected-home EULA and privacy statement describe personal data, cookie, service, and product-data processing.

openness.note: Honeywell Home T9 supports Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Apple HomeKit, and the Resideo app, reducing single-assistant lock-in.

transparency.note: Honeywell Home publishes T9 product, compatibility, sensor, and ENERGY STAR information on public pages.

accessibility.note: T9 supports common central HVAC systems and room sensors, but compatibility and C-wire/power-adapter needs should be checked.

products.name: Drayton Wiser
products.description: A UK smart-heating platform with strong multi-room and OpenTherm support, useful for boiler homes that want more local heating control.

environment.note: Drayton Wiser cites energy-saving potential from direct boiler modulation, smart control, room-by-room control, and smart modes.

privacy.note: Drayton Wiser publishes a privacy policy and data-protection guidance for smart heating controls.

openness.note: Wiser supports Alexa, Google Assistant, IFTTT, and OpenTherm in supported boiler setups.

transparency.note: Drayton Wiser publishes a security support policy naming support periods and security-reporting channels.

accessibility.note: Wiser is strong for compatible UK boiler systems, but kit selection, hub, TRVs, and installation needs make setup less universal.

products.name: Mysa Smart Thermostat
products.description: A specialty smart thermostat for electric baseboard, fan-forced, in-floor, mini-split, and other nonstandard electric heating/cooling setups.

environment.note: Mysa markets smart scheduling, geofencing, utility demand response, and no-subscription control for electric heating and cooling.

privacy.note: Apple's app privacy label for Mysa lists location, contact, identifiers, and usage data among handled data types.

openness.note: Mysa states support for Google Home, Amazon Alexa, and Apple HomeKit.

transparency.note: Mysa publishes product-family and support documentation by heating/cooling type, which helps avoid buying the wrong voltage class.

accessibility.note: Mysa is unusually useful for line-voltage and mini-split situations, but that specialization means it is not a drop-in fit for ordinary central HVAC.

products.name: Sinope Smart Thermostat
products.description: A Canadian smart thermostat specialist for electric baseboard and other line-voltage heating, strongest when that niche matches the home.

environment.note: Sinope says its baseboard thermostat uses schedules, geofencing, TRIAC control, and time-of-use features to reduce unnecessary electric heating.

privacy.note: Sinope publishes privacy and service links on its storefront, but detailed app-data disclosures are less prominent than some competitors.

openness.note: Sinope product pages show SmartThings and Hilo support and describe ecosystem integrations for the thermostat.

transparency.note: Sinope publishes product specifications and compatibility details for electric baseboard thermostats.

accessibility.note: Sinope is helpful for electric-baseboard homes, but line-voltage compatibility makes it unsuitable for ordinary low-voltage central HVAC.

products.name: Amazon Smart Thermostat
products.description: A cheap ENERGY STAR thermostat for Alexa households, with good affordability and a weak privacy/open-ecosystem fit.

environment.note: The ENERGY STAR product finder lists Amazon Smart Thermostat models as certified connected thermostats with demand-response capability.

privacy.note: Mozilla's privacy review highlights Alexa ecosystem dependence and privacy concerns around Amazon smart-home data.

openness.note: Amazon's thermostat is built around Alexa control and requires the Alexa app, making it a weak fit for open-ecosystem values.

transparency.note: Amazon publishes product, setup, and support materials, but the wider Alexa privacy model is harder to evaluate from a thermostat page alone.

accessibility.note: Low price, ENERGY STAR certification, and DIY setup make this one of the most accessible options for compatible 24V HVAC systems.

products.name: Hive Thermostat Mini
products.description: A UK smart-heating option from Centrica/Hive with a low device price, optional service layers, and a mainstream-platform privacy tradeoff.

environment.note: Hive markets the Thermostat Mini around heating-bill and carbon savings, including app control and smart scheduling.

privacy.note: Hive's privacy policy explains how Centrica Hive collects, shares, and uses personal data for Hive services.

openness.note: Hive works with Alexa and Google Assistant, but it is primarily a Hive/Centrica hub-and-app ecosystem rather than an open local-control system.

transparency.note: Hive publishes product pricing, installation, Hive+ renewal notes, and privacy policy pages for customers to inspect.

accessibility.note: The Mini's low purchase price and UK installer path help accessibility, but hub, pro-install, and optional subscription layers add complexity.

products.name: Wyze Thermostat
products.description: A low-cost thermostat for Wyze smart-home users, but weaker on energy-certification confidence and privacy/open-ecosystem values.

environment.note: Wyze's support page says Wyze Thermostat is not ENERGY STAR approved yet, lowering confidence in verified savings.

privacy.note: Wyze's privacy statement covers account, device, usage, app, and service data across the Wyze smart-home ecosystem.

openness.note: Wyze Thermostat is primarily built for the Wyze app ecosystem plus mainstream assistants, not open local control.

transparency.note: Wyze publishes product and support pages, including a direct answer about lack of ENERGY STAR approval.

accessibility.note: Low price and consumer-friendly setup help accessibility for compatible systems, but privacy and certification tradeoffs remain.

products.name: ecobee Smart Thermostat Enhanced
products.description: ecobee's mid-priced model with the Premium's on-device occupancy sensing and wide platform support, under the same Generac-owned privacy notice.

environment.note: ENERGY STAR certified (qualified December 2025) with an occupancy sensor on the device, extra sensor support, geofencing and an optional utility demand-response program. ecobee claims savings of up to 26% a year on heating and cooling.

privacy.note: ecobee's privacy notice says 'Your personal information and data belong to you', but also that ecobee may be treated as selling or sharing data under US state law because it discloses 'certain ecobee Product user data to third parties for their own marketing purposes'. Apple's label lists contact info and user ID linked to you for the developer's marketing.

openness.note: ecobee lists Apple HomeKit, Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Samsung SmartThings and IFTTT support, the same spread as the Premium model.

transparency.note: ecobee shows how its savings figure is calculated (US average heating and cooling cost times the 26% claim) and publishes a dated privacy notice (last revised November 2024) that spells out marketing and utility-program disclosures.

accessibility.note: Sold at $199 with a Power Extender Kit in the box for homes without a C wire, and a compatibility checker online. That is mid-range pricing for a smart thermostat.

products.name: ecobee Smart Thermostat Essential
products.description: ecobee's entry thermostat: ENERGY STAR certified and cheaper, but without the on-device occupancy sensor or SmartThings listing of the higher models.

environment.note: ENERGY STAR lists the Essential under the 'ecobee 7' family (qualified July 2024) with geofencing, humidity sensing and optional extra sensors, but no occupancy sensor on the device. ecobee claims savings of up to 23%.

privacy.note: Covered by the same ecobee notice as the other models: it says your data belongs to you, and also that ecobee discloses certain product user data to third parties for their own marketing purposes. Apple's label lists contact info and user ID used for the developer's marketing.

openness.note: The Essential's own specifications list Google Assistant, Apple HomeKit and Amazon Alexa. SmartThings and IFTTT, listed for the Enhanced and Premium models, are not listed for the Essential.

transparency.note: ecobee states the Essential's specifications, power use (under 3 VA) and data use (5MB a month), and says when the Power Extender Kit is needed.

accessibility.note: Sold at $139. It needs a C wire, or the separately sold Power Extender Kit in some homes, and ecobee offers a compatibility checker and phone support.

products.name: Google Nest Thermostat
products.description: Google's cheaper Nest model: ENERGY STAR certified, easy to fit and Matter-capable, but tied to a Google account, and Google has already cut off older Nest thermostats.

environment.note: ENERGY STAR certified since November 2020 with an occupancy sensor on the device, geofencing and support for utility demand-response programs that the user can opt out of.

privacy.note: Apple's App Store label for the Google Home app, which runs the thermostat, lists search and browsing history linked to you and used for third-party advertising, alongside location, contacts and audio data.

openness.note: The thermostat can connect to up to five other Matter apps, but Google's help page says it can't connect to one 'unless you've added it to your account in the Home app first'.

transparency.note: Google publishes clear end-of-support pages, but it used them to unpair the 1st and 2nd gen Nest Learning Thermostats from its apps on October 25, 2025, ending remote control and security updates. Buyers have no published support end date for this model.

accessibility.note: Sold at $129.99 and designed for DIY install in about 30 minutes. Google says it works with 85% of systems, though some systems need a Nest Power Connector or C wire.

products.name: Google Nest Learning Thermostat (3rd gen, UK/EU)
products.brand: Google, end of line in Europe
products.description: The only Nest Learning Thermostat sold in the UK and Europe, now a last-generation product: Google says it will launch no new Nest thermostats in Europe.

environment.note: The UK Google Store says it learns a schedule, sets itself to Eco temperature when you leave, and its Heat Link uses OpenTherm to modulate condensing boilers. These are manufacturer claims; there is no UK equivalent of the ENERGY STAR field-data certification.

privacy.note: Runs through the same Google Home app as US Nest devices; Apple's label for that app lists search and browsing history linked to you and used for third-party advertising.

openness.note: Google told Which? it will 'no longer launch new Nest thermostats in Europe', so the platform is not being developed for European heating systems. Control is through Google's apps.

transparency.note: Google said the 3rd gen 'will continue to be sold in Europe while supplies last' and will still get security updates, but gave no end date. Older European Nest units were cut off from the app in October 2025.

accessibility.note: Still on sale at £219, but the UK store says it 'should be installed by a professional' with the Heat Link, which adds cost.

products.name: Sensi Lite
products.description: Sensi's cheapest ENERGY STAR model: battery or C-wire powered, with the same no-ad-targeting privacy pledge as the Touch 2.

environment.note: ENERGY STAR certifies the Sensi Lite (ST25, qualified January 2023) with time-of-day, geofencing and humidity features and OpenADR demand-response support. Sensi claims about 23% HVAC energy savings, footnoted with how it was measured.

privacy.note: Sensi says 'we don't use your smart thermostat activity for targeting or advertising purposes' and 'don't sell your personal data to anyone, for any reason'. Apple's label still lists contact info and identifiers used for the developer's own marketing, so the score sits below the Touch 2.

openness.note: Sensi lists Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant and Samsung SmartThings plus its own app. No Apple Home or Matter support is listed.

transparency.note: Sensi's privacy page footnotes how its 23% savings figure was calculated and warns that utility or other third-party programs may collect extra data under their own terms.

accessibility.note: Sensi says no C wire is needed on most systems (heat-only, cool-only and heat pump systems need one). It runs on two AAA batteries and has a 3-year warranty.

products.name: Honeywell Home T6 Pro Z-Wave
products.description: A Z-Wave thermostat with no Wi-Fi or vendor cloud of its own. It is controlled by whichever Z-Wave hub you choose, so it suits Home Assistant and security-panel homes.

environment.note: ENERGY STAR certified (TH6320ZW, qualified April 2023) with an occupancy sensor on the device and geofencing, but the record says demand response is 'Currently not offered', and smart scheduling depends on the hub.

privacy.note: ENERGY STAR lists Z-Wave as its only communication method. There is no Wi-Fi or Resideo app account on the thermostat itself, so data goes only to the hub the owner picks, and privacy depends on that hub.

openness.note: Resideo describes Z-Wave Plus with Z-Wave 5.0 chipset encryption, and scheduling or occupancy control 'through the Z-Wave controller'. Any certified Z-Wave hub can run it, rather than one vendor's cloud.

transparency.note: Resideo's product page publishes system compatibility (3H/2C heat pump, 2H/2C conventional), power options and a 5-year warranty, but it is a professional-channel page with little consumer guidance.

accessibility.note: Needs a separate Z-Wave hub or security panel to be smart at all and is sold mainly through installers, though it can run on 3 AA batteries without a C wire.

products.name: Danfoss Ally
products.description: A Zigbee radiator-valve and room-thermostat system from a large Danish heating maker, for homes with radiators or wet underfloor heating.

environment.note: Danfoss claims 'Up to 30% energy savings' from room-by-room scheduling and remote turn-down. This is a manufacturer claim with no independent test cited on the page.

privacy.note: Apple's label for the Danfoss Ally app says 'The developer does not collect any data from this app', but Danfoss describes Ally as 'cloud based', with 'Cloud data storage with user agreement only'.

openness.note: Danfoss says Ally is Zigbee 3.0 certified and works with Google Assistant and Amazon Alexa, but the app and remote control go through the Danfoss Ally Gateway.

transparency.note: Danfoss publishes its security practices: independent security tests by external specialists, continuous code review, and a channel for reporting vulnerabilities.

accessibility.note: Radiator heads fit with no tools, but the system needs the Ally Gateway plus a head per radiator. The iOS app was last updated in September 2025.

products.name: Eve Thermo
products.description: A battery radiator thermostat that runs over Matter and Thread with no Eve account and no Eve cloud. It needs a Thread hub you may already own.

environment.note: Eve says it lowers the temperature when nobody is home and runs on-device schedules, but it publishes no measured savings figure.

privacy.note: Eve says 'No subscription, no registration', 'No Eve cloud', and that Eve Thermo 'communicates directly with your smartphone or home hub'. Apple's label for the Eve app lists only diagnostics, not linked to the user.

openness.note: Eve Thermo uses Matter over Thread and Eve lists Apple Home, Samsung SmartThings, Amazon Alexa, Home Assistant and Google Home.

transparency.note: Eve's page answers the practical limits openly, for example that on-device schedules are not supported on the Alexa and SmartThings platforms and which valve adapters are included.

accessibility.note: Fits common valves with included Danfoss adapters, but it needs a Matter controller with a Thread border router, and schedules need the Eve app on Apple Home or Google Home.

products.name: Bosch Smart Home Room Thermostat II
products.description: A wall thermostat for Bosch's Smart Home controller system, sold in continental Europe (Bosch's UK webshop is suspended), notable for a published minimum support period per device.

environment.note: Bosch gives no product-specific savings figure. It cites the German Environment Agency's rule of thumb that 1 degree lower saves about 6% of energy, and says its thermostats set temperatures to 0.5 degrees.

privacy.note: Apple's label for the Bosch Smart Home app lists only email address as data linked to you. Usage data and device ID are collected but not linked to the user.

openness.note: Bosch lists Room thermostat II among the devices whose functions can be used in any Matter system, and says Matter devices communicate locally and in encrypted form. It still depends on the Bosch Smart Home Controller.

transparency.note: Bosch guarantees 'a minimum operating period of four years', counted from the earlier of installation or the last date the device was sold in its shop, covering software and security updates, server functions and support, and publishes end dates per device.

accessibility.note: Sold at 79.95 euros in Germany, but Bosch says it can only be used together with the Bosch Smart Home Controller, which adds cost for a first-time buyer.

products.name: Mysa Smart Thermostat for Central HVAC
products.description: Mysa's first thermostat for ordinary 24V central heating and cooling: ENERGY STAR certified, Matter certified and subscription-free, but it needs a C wire.

environment.note: ENERGY STAR certified in October 2025 with geofencing, humidity sensing and demand-response support. Mysa claims 15-26% heating savings.

privacy.note: Mysa says 'We never sell your data to third parties', but control requires a free Mysa app account, and Apple's label for the Mysa app (scored on the existing Mysa entry) lists location, contact and identifier data.

openness.note: Mysa says it is 'Matter certified' and connects to Apple Home, Google Home, Amazon Alexa and other Matter platforms 'with no extra hub required'.

transparency.note: Mysa states that software updates stay free for the life of the device, that there are no subscription paywalls, and gives a 5-year warranty and full compatibility specifications.

accessibility.note: Priced from $129 for central systems, but it requires a C wire, or Mysa's separately sold C-Wire Power Adapter on two-wire systems.
